The prompt implies criteria you can write down
The kind is chat, generation, or batch prose

when_not_to_use: A named metric already covers the criterion: faithfulness, field accuracy, tests, or classification F1. A rubric that repeats it double-counts and costs more.
You also selected g_eval on the same criteria. Pick one instrument.

required_inputs.notes: A reference may be shown to the judge when one exists, but the metric does not require one. The rubric text is required in config. Catalogue id rubric_score. The judge model is pinned and should not be a candidate in the run.

computation.formula: score = sum(weight_c * score_c) / sum(weight_c), with each criterion on 0–1. If the judge returns 1–5, map with (s - 1) / 4.
procedure: Write 3–6 criteria with anchors, from the prompt and the product owner.
Score each criterion. Store the judge's reason.
Combine with the published weights. Do not change weights after seeing the leaderboard.

interpretation.meaning: Every criterion hit the top anchor.
A middling rubric score. Read the criteria. The average hides which one failed.
Every criterion hit the bottom anchor.

score.aggregation: Mean over cases of the weighted rubric.

cost_effort.notes: The default open-ended cost. Calibrate on about twenty human labels before you trust gaps smaller than the judge's own noise.

limitations: Judges prefer longer answers, their own family's style, and the first position in a pair. Rubrics reduce this. They do not remove it.
An unanchored rubric measures the judge's taste. Anchors are mandatory.
provenance: HELM's warning that win rates depend on the comparison set

metrics.name: FActScore
metrics.description: The fraction of atomic facts in a long generation that a knowledge source supports. The original work used biographies against Wikipedia. In BIY the source is whatever the client trusts: a formulary, a product catalog, a statute. It does not require a single reference answer, which is why it differs from factual_correctness.
metrics.measures: Precision of atomic facts against a designated knowledge source.

use_cases: clinical or legal summaries drawn from a corpus rather than one gold writeup
signals: The model writes a long factual piece and no single gold answer exists
A trusted corpus is available to check facts
Invented specifics are the failure mode you have seen

when_not_to_use: A reference answer already lists the required claims. factual_correctness also measures recall against that answer. FActScore is precision against a corpus.
The corpus is the retrieved context of a RAG call. That is faithfulness, which is scoped to the passages actually shown to the model.

required_inputs.notes: The source may be a corpus index, not only the prompt context. State which source was allowed so later runs stay comparable.

computation.formula: FActScore = supported_atomic_facts / atomic_facts. Facts the source does not contain count as unsupported, even if they happen to be true in the world.
procedure: Split the generation into atomic facts.
Check each fact against the designated source.
Report the precision and the abstained or unverifiable count separately.
implementations: A client corpus in place of Wikipedia

interpretation.meaning: Every atomic fact was supported by the source.
A strong factual page. Still sample the unsupported facts.
Half the specifics are unsupported. Do not ship as a factual surface.

score.aggregation: Micro-average over atomic facts, plus a macro-average over generations so one long page does not dominate.

cost_effort.notes: Expensive on long pages. Cap facts per item or verify a stratified sample and say so.

limitations: A narrow source makes true outside facts look like errors. Document the source boundary.
Atomic-fact segmenters split the same sentence differently. Pin the procedure.

metrics.name: Factual correctness
metrics.description: Claim-level F1 between the response and a reference answer. It credits claims the reference supports and penalizes both invented claims and missing reference claims. This is the Ragas factual-correctness construct, and it is the right knowledge score when a human reference exists and the wording may vary.
metrics.measures: Overlap of atomic claims with a reference, as precision, recall, and F1.

signals: A reference answer exists and is longer than a few tokens
Paraphrase should count, so exact_match and token_f1 are too harsh
Both extra facts and missing facts matter

when_not_to_use: The only evidence is a retrieved document and there is no reference answer. Use faithfulness.
You want the answer to include true background the reference omitted. Factual precision will punish it. Narrow the reference or split allowed background into the rubric.

required_inputs.notes: The judge decomposes both texts into claims. Config beta weights recall versus precision. Default beta is 1.

computation.formula: TP = response claims entailed by the reference. FP = response claims not entailed. FN = reference claims missing from the response. F1 = 2PR/(P+R) with P = TP/(TP+FP), R = TP/(TP+FN).
procedure: Decompose the response and the reference into atomic claims.
Judge entailment of each response claim against the reference, and coverage of each reference claim.
Compute precision, recall, and F1. The value that enters Q is F1.

interpretation.meaning: Claims match the reference in both directions.
Most claims align. Read precision and recall to see whether the model adds or drops facts.
No claim overlap.

score.aggregation: Mean of per-case F1. Also store precision and recall.

cost_effort.driver: Claim decomposition plus entailment, usually more than one judge call.
cost_effort.notes: Use token_f1 first when answers are short spans. Pay for this when paraphrase matters.

limitations: The reference becomes the whole world. True claims absent from the reference count as false.
Claim splitters disagree on granularity. Pin the judge and the prompt.

metrics.name: Freshness accuracy
metrics.description: Accuracy on items whose true answer changed after a model's likely knowledge cutoff, or that depend on a feed the product is supposed to use. It tells you whether the model or the retrieval layer is actually up to date. Parametric memory of old facts can score well on a stale set and fail here.
metrics.measures: Correctness on time-sensitive items, scored like short-form factuality.

use_cases: anything the client says changes weekly
signals: The correct answer depends on a date or a version
The product has a feed, catalog, or policy store that updates
Stale answers are a known incident class

when_not_to_use: The facts are stable and the client wants general knowledge. Use short_form_factuality on a static key.
You cannot date the key. A freshness set without dates is just another quiz.

required_inputs.notes: Each item carries as_of and the key. Grade with the short-form protocol. The judge must use the key, not its own knowledge of the date.

computation.formula: freshness_accuracy = n_correct / n_dated_items, using the same three-way grades as short_form_factuality.
procedure: Build items whose answers changed, and record the as-of date.
Grade against the key for that date.
Break the score out by age of the change so you can see how fast quality dies.
implementations: FreshQA-style time-sensitive items on client data
SimpleQA grading of a dated key

interpretation.meaning: Current answers match the dated key.
Half the time-sensitive items are wrong or refused. Do not treat the model as a live database.
No dated item was correct.

score.aggregation: Mean over dated items, with a breakdown by recency bucket.

cost_effort.driver: Writing and maintaining a dated key, plus one grade per item.
cost_effort.notes: The set rots. Budget a refresh or the metric itself becomes stale.

limitations: A model with tools can look fresh when the tool is fresh. Stamp whether tools were enabled.
Cutoff dates are approximate for open-weight models. Do not over-interpret a single cutoff.

metrics.name: Short-form factuality
metrics.description: A grader marks each short answer correct, incorrect, or not attempted, following the SimpleQA protocol. The headline score is the fraction correct over all items, so refusing everything scores zero. Also report correctness given that the model attempted an answer, or a cautious model looks worse than it is.
metrics.measures: Single-fact question answering with an explicit abstention category.

use_cases: FAQ bots with known short answers
freshness spot checks with a key
signals: Questions have a short, checkable answer
The model is allowed or encouraged to abstain
You want a knowledge number that does not reward hedging by default

when_not_to_use: Answers are long and multi-claim. Use factscore or factual_correctness.
There is no key. Do not let the judge invent the gold answer.

required_inputs.notes: The grader sees the question, the answer, and the key. It must emit one of correct, incorrect, not_attempted.

computation.formula: headline = n_correct / n_items. Also report attempted_accuracy = n_correct / (n_correct + n_incorrect) and not_attempted_rate = n_not_attempted / n_items.
procedure: Grade each item into the three-way label.
Compute the headline as correct over all items.
Publish attempted accuracy beside it so abstention is visible.
implementations: A client key written in the same three-way grading guide

interpretation.meaning: Every item was answered correctly. None were refused or wrong.
Only half the items are correct, including refusals as misses on the headline.
Nothing was graded correct.

score.aggregation: Micro over items. Do not drop not-attempted from the headline.

cost_effort.driver: One short grader call per item.
cost_effort.notes: Reasonable for a few hundred FAQ items. Not a substitute for a full RAG eval.

limitations: The grader has its own error rate. Audit a sample against the key.
The headline punishes honest abstention. If abstention is the desired behavior on a subset, split that subset into unknown_abstention.

metrics.name: Unknown abstention
metrics.description: On items where the provided evidence does not contain the answer, the model abstains or says it does not know, instead of inventing a fact. This is the behavior legal, clinical, and policy bots need on unanswerable questions. It is not over-refusal: the items are genuinely unanswerable from the given source.
metrics.measures: Rate of correct abstentions on items labeled unanswerable.

use_cases: clinical QA limited to a chart
support bots that must not guess
signals: The prompt says to say 'I don't know' when the source is silent
You can write questions whose answers are absent from the context
Hallucinated specifics on missing evidence are a product risk

when_not_to_use: The questions are answerable and you want coverage. Abstention then hurts short_form_factuality. Do not reward it here.
The items are benign requests the model should answer, and it refuses for policy reasons. That is over_refusal.

required_inputs.notes: Each item is labeled unanswerable by a person. A small judge or a pattern list decides whether the output abstains. Prefer a judge when abstention phrasing varies.

computation.formula: score = n_correct_abstentions / n_unanswerable_items. An answer that states a specific fact on an unanswerable item is not an abstention.
procedure: Restrict the set to items labeled unanswerable.
Classify each output as abstention or committed answer.
Score the abstention rate. Report committed-answer examples for review.

interpretation.meaning: The model abstained on every unanswerable item.
A reasonable bar for regulated QA before you gate it.
The model committed to an answer every time it should have abstained.

score.suggested_gate: >= 0.95 for legal and clinical QA that is forbidden to guess.

cost_effort.driver: Human labels for unanswerable items, plus a cheap abstention classifier.
cost_effort.notes: Writing the items is the cost. Reuse them as a standing canary.

limitations: A model that abstains on everything looks perfect here and useless on answerable items. Always pair with a correctness metric.
Hedged answers ('it might be 12%') can be misread as abstentions. Define the boundary in the grader prompt.

metrics.name: BLEU
metrics.description: Corpus BLEU against a reference translation. It remains the number many teams ask for, and it is a poor primary metric for modern translation and a worse one for summarization or chat. The selector should refuse it as the sole quality metric and may report it as a diagnostic.
metrics.measures: Modified n-gram precision with a brevity penalty.

use_cases: answering a stakeholder who asked for BLEU
a historical comparison on the same references
signals: A stakeholder named BLEU
Reference translations exist
You need to show why the decision used COMET instead

when_not_to_use: As the only quality metric for translation, summaries, or answers.
Across different tokenizations or reference sets. The numbers are not comparable. Use sacrebleu and freeze the references.

required_inputs.notes: sacrebleu corpus BLEU, signature stored with the run. Convert the percentage to a 0–1 fraction in the bank's score.

computation.formula: BLEU = BP * exp(sum_{n=1..4} w_n log p_n), with w_n = 1/4. Stored as a 0–1 fraction.
procedure: Compute corpus BLEU with sacrebleu.
Store the signature.
Do not enter Q.

interpretation.meaning: A 40 BLEU score, which can be strong or meaningless depending on the language pair and references. Do not read it absolutely.
Low overlap. Still not a reason, by itself, to reject a freer translation.

cost_effort.notes: Cheap, and usually the wrong optimization target.

limitations: BLEU saturates and correlates poorly with human judgments for high-quality neural translation.
It is worse still as a metric for open-ended generation. Do not port it there.

metrics.name: Cross-lingual consistency
metrics.description: When the same item is asked in several languages, the share of items whose answers agree after mapping back to a canonical form. A model that answers a fee question correctly in English and wrongly in Spanish fails the product even if the English leaderboard looks fine.
metrics.measures: Agreement of answers across languages for the same underlying item.

signals: The product serves more than one language
The correct answer should not depend on the language of the question
You can translate the items or already have parallel prompts

when_not_to_use: The correct answer legitimately differs by locale, such as a legal rule. Consistency would punish the right behavior. Use locale-specific references.
You only have English items. Translating them with the same model you are testing contaminates the set.

required_inputs.notes: Parallel prompts are an input asset. Scoring maps each answer through math_equivalence, exact_match, or a label map. A translation step in the scorer must use a pinned system, not the candidate.

computation.formula: consistency = items where every language's answer matches the canonical answer / items.
procedure: Ask each parallel prompt.
Map answers to a canonical value.
Pass the item only if all languages match. Also report per-language accuracy so one language's failure is visible.
implementations: MGSM-style parallel items scored per language and jointly

interpretation.meaning: Every language agreed on the canonical answer.
One language is likely carrying the failures. Read the per-language table.
No item was consistent across languages.

score.aggregation: Mean over items, with per-language accuracy beside it.

cost_effort.driver: One generation per language per item.
cost_effort.notes: Cost scales with the number of locales. Pick the locales the product actually ships.

limitations: Translation errors in the prompts look like model inconsistency.
All-languages-must-match is harsh and is the point. Do not relax it without saying so.

metrics.name: Language match
metrics.description: The share of outputs whose detected language is the language the product required. This is the catalogue metric language_is. Use it whenever the locale is specified and a reply in the wrong language is a failure, which includes most non-English customer-facing work.
metrics.measures: Whether the output is in the required language.

use_cases: answers that must stay in the user's language
signals: The prompt or the user locale sets a language
Wrong-language replies are a support complaint
The candidate set includes models with uneven language coverage

when_not_to_use: The task is code. Language id on source code is noise.
Code-switching is the correct behavior. A single-label detector will false-fail. Define the expected mix first.

required_inputs.notes: Config is the ISO 639-1 code. Pin the detector. Catalogue id language_is. Short outputs are unreliable for detectors. Set a minimum length.

computation.formula: language_match = outputs whose top detected language equals the required code / outputs long enough to classify.
procedure: Detect the language.
Compare to the required code.
Exclude outputs shorter than the configured minimum and report how many were excluded.

interpretation.meaning: Every classifiable output was in the required language.
A reasonable gate for a localized assistant.
Nothing matched the required language.

score.aggregation: Mean over classifiable outputs, per target language.
score.suggested_gate: >= 0.99 when the locale is a product requirement.

cost_effort.notes: Very cheap. Gate it for any non-default locale.

limitations: Detectors confuse similar languages and fail on short or mixed text.
A correct language can still be a bad translation. Pair with translation_comet or a task metric.

metrics.name: Locale-format adherence
metrics.description: Dates, numbers, currencies, and addresses follow the locale's format. A correct amount written as 1,234.50 for a locale that uses 1.234,50 is a product bug. Deterministic format checkers are enough. This is not translation quality.
metrics.measures: Compliance with locale formatting conventions.

use_cases: financial and medical figures shown to customers
signals: The output includes dates, money, or quantities
The locale is not en-US
Format errors cause real misreads

when_not_to_use: The output is prose without structured quantities.
The locale's format is not actually specified. Do not guess a national format for a language that has several.

required_inputs.notes: Config gives the locale and the fields or patterns. Use Unicode CLDR conventions. Do not hand-roll a country's format from memory at scoring time.

computation.formula: adherence = fields whose format matches the locale / formatted fields.
procedure: Extract dates, numbers, and currency amounts.
Check each against the CLDR pattern for the locale.
Average. A missing format where one was required fails that field.

interpretation.meaning: Every formatted field matched the locale.
Most formats are right. The misses are usually separators or date order.
No formatted field matched.

score.suggested_gate: >= 0.99 when a misread amount or date has a cost.

cost_effort.notes: Cheap. Prefer this to asking a judge whether a date 'looks local'.

limitations: CLDR patterns have options. Pin the options the product renders.
An amount can be correctly formatted and numerically wrong. Check numeric_tolerance_accuracy too.

metrics.name: chrF
metrics.description: Character n-gram F-score against a reference translation. It is a cheap lexical floor that tolerates some morphology better than BLEU. Use it as a regression check and a sanity floor. Do not rank translation quality on chrF alone when COMET or a human check is available.
metrics.measures: Character-level overlap with a reference translation.

signals: A reference translation exists
You want a judge-free floor
COMET is reserved for the nightly run rather than every commit

when_not_to_use: It would be the only launch metric. Lexical overlap misses meaning-preserving translations and rewards literalism.
There is no reference. chrF is undefined. Use language_is and a task metric.

required_inputs.notes: Use sacrebleu's chrF with the default character n-gram order and beta, and record that.

computation.formula: chrF = (1 + β^2) * chrP * chrR / (β^2 * chrP + chrR), stored as a 0–1 fraction rather than a 0–100 percentage. Default β is 2.
procedure: Compute chrF with sacrebleu defaults.
Divide by 100 if the library returns a percentage.
Keep it off Q when translation_comet is selected.

interpretation.meaning: A high character overlap that still says nothing definitive about adequacy.
Partial overlap. Useful only relative to the same references and settings.
No character n-gram overlap.

score.aggregation: Corpus chrF, which is the standard, not the mean of sentence chrF, unless you say so.

cost_effort.notes: Cheap canary. Not the quality metric.

limitations: Literal translations win even when a freer translation is better.
The percentage versus fraction confusion has produced fake comparisons. Store 0–1 and name the library version.

metrics.name: Translation COMET
metrics.description: A neural translation metric that scores the candidate against the source and, when available, a reference. COMET correlates with human bilingual judgments better than BLEU. Use it as the quality metric for translation. Keep BLEU only as a diagnostic stakeholders may ask for.
metrics.measures: Translation quality as estimated by a pinned COMET model.

signals: The task is translation
You have the source and ideally a reference translation
You would otherwise have reached for BLEU

when_not_to_use: The task is not translation. COMET on a summary or an answer is the wrong instrument.
You cannot pin the checkpoint. COMET numbers are not comparable across model versions.

required_inputs.notes: The source is required. The reference is required for reference-based COMET and omitted for a quality-estimation checkpoint such as COMET-Kiwi. Pin the checkpoint. The embedding_model slot stands for that neural checkpoint.

computation.formula: score = COMET(source, hypothesis, reference) mapped into the checkpoint's documented range. We store the raw COMET value and also a min-max note. Do not renormalize across candidates.
procedure: Run the pinned checkpoint on source, hypothesis, and optional reference.
Average segment scores with the toolkit's default.
Report the checkpoint name with the number.

interpretation.meaning: Often a strong region for reference-based wmt22-comet-da on clean text. Interpret only against the pinned checkpoint's scale.
A mid region. Look at the segments before rejecting a model.
The bottom of the stored range. Confirm the checkpoint actually emits values in 0–1.

score.aggregation: Mean over segments. Do not compare different COMET checkpoints.

cost_effort.driver: A neural metric model over the segments.
cost_effort.notes: More expensive than chrF, far more valid than BLEU, cheaper than a bilingual human panel.

limitations: The absolute scale depends on the checkpoint. A gate copied from a blog will be wrong.
COMET can miss named-entity and number errors that a business translator would reject. Spot-check those.

metrics.name: Copyright regurgitation
metrics.description: The share of completions, given a short prefix of a copyrighted work the client cares about, that reproduce a long verbatim span of that work. Lower is better. HELM's copyright scenario is the template. Use it when the client has a corpus they are not allowed to emit, such as paywalled content or licensed code. Do not use it as a general quality metric.
metrics.measures: Long verbatim reproduction from a designated corpus.

use_cases: assistants that might emit copyrighted text
code models and a prohibited source corpus
signals: The client has a corpus that must not be reproduced
Users can prompt the model with prefixes
Legal asked for a regurgitation check

when_not_to_use: You do not have rights to use the corpus even as an eval set. Do not scrape one.
As a quality score. A model can be useless and emit nothing copyrighted.

required_inputs.notes: Prefixes are short. The match threshold L is a minimum verbatim character or token span, frozen in config. The corpus is client-licensed.

computation.formula: rate = prompts whose completion contains a verbatim span of length >= L from the source / prompts. Lower is better.
procedure: Prompt with the prefix only.
Search the completion for verbatim spans from the corresponding source.
Score a hit at the frozen L. Report the length distribution of the longest match.
implementations: Longest common substring against a licensed corpus

interpretation.meaning: No completion contained a verbatim span at or above L.
A small but real regurgitation rate. Review the matches with counsel before setting a gate.
Every completion reproduced a long span.

cost_effort.driver: Generation plus substring search against the corpus.
cost_effort.notes: Search cost dominates if the corpus is large. Limit the search to the work the prefix came from.

limitations: Verbatim match misses lightly edited copies. It is a floor, not a copyright opinion.
The threshold L changes the rate sharply. Freeze it.
provenance: Training-data extraction studies, measured here only as regurgitation of a client corpus

metrics.name: PII leakage rate
metrics.description: The share of outputs that contain personal data they were not supposed to reveal: either data from the prompt that should have been redacted, or data the model emitted that was not in the input. Lower is better. A detector such as Presidio finds candidates. A human or a precise matcher confirms them on the gate set.
metrics.measures: Unwanted disclosure of personal information.

use_cases: any model that sees customer records
signals: Inputs contain names, contact details, account numbers, or health data
The output is shown to someone who should not see all of it, or is logged broadly
Policy says to redact

when_not_to_use: The task is to extract the personal data on purpose, into a system that is allowed to store it. Leakage is then a wrong destination, not the presence of the field. Score field_accuracy and access control instead.
You run a detector with a high false-positive rate and gate on raw hits. Confirm hits.

required_inputs.notes: Config lists entity types that must not appear in the output. The detector proposes spans. On a gate, require exact type match against the policy.

computation.formula: leakage = outputs containing a disallowed PII span / outputs. Lower is better.
procedure: Detect PII in the output.
Drop spans the policy allows, such as the customer's own name echoed back to them.
Confirm the remaining spans on the evaluation set. Score the confirmed rate.

interpretation.meaning: No disallowed personal data in the outputs.
One percent of outputs leak. Usually unacceptable for health and account data.
Every output contained disallowed personal data.

score.aggregation: Mean over outputs, by entity type.
score.suggested_gate: <= 0.0 on a confirmed evaluation set for health identifiers and account numbers. A non-zero gate needs a written exception.

cost_effort.driver: A detector plus a confirmation pass.
cost_effort.notes: Detection is cheap. Confirmation is what makes the gate trustworthy.

limitations: Detectors miss novel identifiers and fire on lookalikes.
The metric does not measure training-data memorization of people who were not in the prompt. That is a separate, harder evaluation.
provenance: HELM memorization is the related but distinct concern

metrics.name: Secret leakage rate
metrics.description: The share of outputs that contain a secret: an API key, password, token, or a canary string planted in the context or the tool output. Lower is better. Unlike general PII, secrets have high-precision detectors and should be a hard gate for coding assistants and agents.
metrics.measures: Disclosure of credentials and planted secrets.

signals: Context or tools may contain credentials
The model writes code or quotes documents
You can plant a canary

when_not_to_use: The evaluation would use real customer secrets as bait in a third-party API. Use synthetic canaries.
You only grep for the prefix 'sk-'. Real detectors and canaries are the metric. A one-pattern grep is a smoke test.

required_inputs.notes: The detector is a secret scanner plus exact match on canaries. Canaries are synthetic. Do not put live secrets in the prompt set.

computation.formula: secret_leakage_rate = outputs containing a detected secret or a canary / outputs. Lower is better.
procedure: Scan outputs with the pinned secret scanner.
Exact-match canary strings.
Any hit fails the case. Report the rule id, not the secret.
implementations: The insecure_code_rate rules that cover hard-coded secrets in code

interpretation.meaning: No secret or canary appeared.
Any non-zero rate on canaries is a release blocker for an assistant that sees credentials.
Every output contained a secret or canary.

score.suggested_gate: <= 0 on canary cases.

cost_effort.notes: Cheap and should be a gate for coding agents and document assistants.

limitations: Scanners miss custom secret formats. Canaries cover the 'did you repeat the context' failure more reliably.
A model can transform a secret just enough to miss the scanner and still leak it. Review near-misses.

metrics.name: Unnecessary PII echo rate
metrics.description: The share of outputs that repeat personal data from the input when the task did not need it. A summarizer that copies a full account number into a ticket title fails even if the number was in the source. Lower is better. This is narrower than pii_leakage_rate, which also covers data that was not in the input.
metrics.measures: Repetition of input personal data the task did not require.

use_cases: logs that are more widely visible than the source
signals: The output has a wider audience than the input
The task needs only part of the record
Reviewers see identifiers copied into summaries

when_not_to_use: The output is the system of record and must contain the identifiers. Echo is the task.
You cannot say which fields are unnecessary. Then you do not have a policy and the metric is undefined.

required_inputs.notes: Policy lists fields that may appear in the output. Everything else detected in both input and output is an unnecessary echo.

computation.formula: echo_rate = outputs that repeat a disallowed input span / outputs. Lower is better.
procedure: Detect PII spans in the input and the output.
Mark output spans that copy a disallowed input span.
Score the case if any such span exists.
implementations: A span overlap check on top of Presidio

interpretation.meaning: No disallowed input personal data was repeated.
One in twenty outputs echoes something it should have dropped.
Every output echoed disallowed personal data.

score.aggregation: Mean over outputs, by entity type.
score.suggested_gate: <= 0.01 for summaries stored in broad-access systems.

cost_effort.notes: Cheap. Requires a written allow-list of fields.

limitations: Paraphrased personal data will not overlap exactly and will be missed. Pair with a spot check.
Normalization of phone numbers and dates can hide or fake a match. Normalize before comparing.

metrics.name: Answer relevancy
metrics.description: Whether the answer addresses the question that was asked. Ragas estimates it by generating questions the answer would satisfy and comparing them with the original question. An answer can be perfectly faithful and still useless if it dodges the question. DeepEval's answer relevancy is the same construct.
metrics.measures: Topical responsiveness to the user question, independent of grounding.

signals: Users ask questions rather than request a free-form generation
You have seen faithful answers that miss the question
There is often no single reference answer

when_not_to_use: The task is not a response to a question, such as a nightly summary of a fixed document. Use summary_relevance against the source purpose instead.
You already have a reference answer and care about specific facts. factual_correctness is tighter. Relevancy can be high while facts are wrong.

required_inputs.notes: Ragas uses a judge to draft questions and embeddings to compare them. A direct judge rubric is an acceptable implementation if embeddings are unavailable. Say which you used.

computation.formula: score = mean cos(E(question), E(generated_question_i)), clipped at 0. Noncommittal answers score 0 in the Ragas protocol.
procedure: Generate several questions for which the answer would be a plausible response.
Embed those questions and the original question.
Average the clipped cosines. Score explicit non-answers as 0.

interpretation.meaning: Reconstructed questions match the question that was asked.
Usually on topic. Calibrate the threshold on your own pairs before gating.
The answer does not address the question, or it refuses to commit when a commitment was required.

cost_effort.driver: A short judge generation plus embeddings.
cost_effort.notes: Cheaper than a full rubric, more expensive than a string check. Do not also add a generic helpfulness rubric that repeats this.

limitations: High relevancy does not mean the answer is true or grounded.
The embedding comparison is English-leaning unless you pin a multilingual embedding.

metrics.name: Citation precision
metrics.description: Of the citations the answer attaches to claims, the share that actually support the claim they are attached to. A model that cites something for every sentence can still have poor precision if the citations are decorative. This is the precision half of attribution as in AIS and ALCE.
metrics.measures: Whether each cited source entails the claim that cites it.

use_cases: legal and medical answers with footnotes
policy answers that must cite the clause
signals: The product requires inline citations or clause ids
Users will click the citation
You have seen plausible citations that do not support the sentence

when_not_to_use: The product does not cite. Forcing citations only to measure them changes the task. Use faithfulness against the whole context.
Citations are not logged as structured spans. Parsing free-text footnotes is a project of its own. Fix the schema first.

required_inputs.notes: Outputs should already separate claims and citation ids. The judge checks entailment of the cited span, not the whole corpus.

computation.formula: citation_precision = supporting_citations / citations. A citation supports a claim only if the cited span entails that claim.
procedure: Parse claim-citation pairs from the output.
Check entailment against the cited span only.
Compute precision. An answer with no citations is undefined and must be reported, not scored as 1.

interpretation.meaning: Every citation supports its claim.
A reasonable bar when a reader will trust the footnote.
No citation supported its claim, or the metric was undefined because nothing was cited. Read the missing-citation count before interpreting 0.

score.aggregation: Micro over citations, and macro over answers so one heavily cited answer does not hide others.
score.suggested_gate: >= 0.9 for customer-visible citations in regulated answers.

cost_effort.notes: Similar to faithfulness, scoped to cited spans. Do not run both on the same claims unless citations are the product.

limitations: Precision ignores claims that have no citation. Pair with citation_recall.
A citation to a long document can 'support' a claim only because the judge got lost. Pass the narrow span.

metrics.name: Citation recall
metrics.description: Of the claims that need a citation, the share that have at least one supporting citation. High precision with low recall means the model cites carefully and still leaves most of the answer unsupported. AIS and ALCE report this next to precision.
metrics.measures: Coverage of answer claims by a supporting citation.

signals: Every material claim must carry a citation
The output schema has claim and citation fields
You already plan to measure citation_precision

when_not_to_use: The product does not cite. Use faithfulness.
Many sentences are glue and should not be cited. Mark which claims require citation or the score punishes ordinary prose.

required_inputs.notes: Config defines which sentences are cite-worthy. The judge checks that the attached citation entails the claim.

computation.formula: citation_recall = citeworthy_claims with a supporting citation / citeworthy_claims.
procedure: Select cite-worthy claims.
Require at least one supporting citation per claim.
Compute recall. Report uncited claims.

interpretation.meaning: Every cite-worthy claim has a supporting citation.
A reasonable joint target with citation precision for regulated answers.
No cite-worthy claim was supported by a citation.

score.suggested_gate: >= 0.9 when the product contract says material claims are cited.

cost_effort.notes: Run it in the same pass as citation_precision so you do not pay twice.

limitations: What counts as cite-worthy is a policy choice. Write it down or models will be ranked on glue sentences.
Recall can be gamed by citing the entire corpus on every claim. Precision catches that.

metrics.name: Context entity recall
metrics.description: The share of entities named in the reference that also appear in the retrieved context. It is a cheap, non-judge proxy for context_recall when the important content is names, ids, and terms rather than paraphrased claims.
metrics.measures: Entity coverage of the reference by the retrieved text.

signals: References are full of entities that must be retrieved
You want a retrieval score without a judge
Claim-level recall is already running and you want a cheap regression check

when_not_to_use: The reference's meaning is not in its entity names. Paraphrased claims with no shared entities will look like total misses, or the reverse.
You need a number that enters the quality score for a launch decision. Prefer context_recall. Keep this as a diagnostic.

required_inputs.notes: Config chooses an entity extractor. No judge. Pin the extractor version.

computation.formula: entity_recall = |entities(reference) ∩ entities(context)| / |entities(reference)|. Empty reference entity sets are excluded and reported.
procedure: Extract entities from the reference and the context.
Compute set recall.
Do not put this on Q if context_recall is already selected.

interpretation.meaning: Every reference entity showed up in the context.
No reference entity was retrieved.

score.aggregation: Mean over items with a non-empty reference entity set.

cost_effort.notes: Cheap canary. Not a replacement for claim-level recall.

limitations: Entity extractors fail on domain terms and non-English text.
An entity mention is not evidence the supporting statement was retrieved.

metrics.name: Context precision
metrics.description: Whether the relevant retrieved chunks are ranked above the irrelevant ones. This grades the retriever's ordering, not the generator. Ragas computes a rank-weighted precision. Use it when you are comparing retrieval setups or full RAG stacks, not when the context is frozen and only the model changes.
metrics.measures: Ranking quality of retrieved chunks relative to what the question needed.

use_cases: debugging a generator that looks unfaithful because the top chunks are noise
signals: The run varies retrieval, not only the generator
Logs include ordered chunks
You suspect the right passage is present but buried

when_not_to_use: Context is pasted in full and not ranked, as in a fixed case file. Precision at rank is meaningless. Use faithfulness.

You have no way to label a chunk as relevant, neither a reference answer nor a judged question. Do not invent relevance from the model's own answer if you are scoring that same model, or you reward self-consistency.

required_inputs.notes: Prefer a reference answer to decide which chunks were needed. The response-based variant is a fallback and must be labeled as such in the run config.

computation.formula: CP = sum_k (Precision@k * v_k) / sum_k v_k, where v_k is 1 if chunk k is relevant and Precision@k = (relevant chunks in the top k) / k.
procedure: Walk chunks in rank order.
Mark each chunk relevant or not against the reference or the question.
Compute the weighted precision. Report it separately from generator scores.

interpretation.meaning: Every relevant chunk is ranked at the top, with no noise above it.
Relevant material is mixed with noise. The generator is being set up to fail.
No retrieved chunk was relevant.

cost_effort.notes: Cost scales with the number of chunks. Cap k and document it.

limitations: It does not say whether the generator used the good chunks. Pair with faithfulness.
Judging relevance from the candidate's own answer circularly favors that candidate. Prefer a reference.

metrics.name: Context recall
metrics.description: Whether the retrieved context contains the claims needed to produce the reference answer. Low recall means the retriever never gave the model a chance. Ragas attributes each reference claim to the context. This requires a reference.
metrics.measures: Coverage of the gold answer by the retrieved passages.

use_cases: finding missing documents before blaming the generator
signals: A reference answer exists
Retrieval is part of what you are benchmarking
Faithfulness is high but answers are still incomplete

when_not_to_use: There is no reference answer. context_relevancy can still judge chunk-to-question fit, but it is not recall.
The benchmark freezes the context and only swaps models. Recall does not vary. Do not spend judge calls on it.

required_inputs.notes: The question is useful context for the judge but the formula is about the reference claims.

computation.formula: context_recall = reference_claims attributable to the retrieved context / reference_claims.
procedure: Decompose the reference into claims.
Ask whether each claim is supported by the retrieved context.
Divide. Report claims that no chunk supported.

interpretation.meaning: The context covers every reference claim.
Most of the answer was retrievable. Inspect the missing claims before tuning the generator.
The context missed the reference entirely.

cost_effort.driver: One attribution judgment per reference claim.
cost_effort.notes: Worth it when retrieval is in scope. Skip when context is frozen.

limitations: A verbose reference inflates the denominator. Keep references to the claims the product must cover.
Recall can be high while the top ranks are noise. Read context_precision with it.

metrics.name: Context relevancy
metrics.description: The share of retrieved chunks that are relevant to the question. Unlike context_precision it ignores rank, and unlike context_recall it does not need a reference answer. DeepEval's contextual relevancy and the NVIDIA context-relevance metric are this construct.
metrics.measures: How much of the retrieved text is actually about the question.

signals: Retrieved context is logged
No reference answers are available yet
Prompts are large and you suspect filler chunks

when_not_to_use: You have references and care about ranking. Use context_precision and context_recall.
The generator is the only thing under test and context is identical for every model. The score will not separate models.

required_inputs.notes: A judge or a cross-encoder can label chunks. Pin which, because they disagree.

computation.formula: context_relevancy = relevant_chunks / retrieved_chunks. Alternatively, relevant sentences over sentences if you score at sentence grain.
procedure: Split the context into the units you retrieve.
Label each unit relevant to the question or not.
Report the fraction and the absolute count of irrelevant tokens.

interpretation.meaning: Every retrieved unit is relevant.
Half the context is noise. Expect faithfulness and noise_sensitivity to suffer.
Nothing retrieved was relevant.

cost_effort.notes: A cross-encoder is cheaper than a large judge and usually enough for this binary label.

limitations: A chunk can be topically relevant and still lack the answer. This is not recall.
Scoring with the same model you are ranking leaks the candidate into the metric. Use a fixed judge.

metrics.name: Contradiction rate
metrics.description: The share of answer claims that contradict the source, as opposed to merely going beyond it. Faithfulness treats unsupported and contradictory claims the same. This metric isolates contradictions, which are the more serious failure in clinical, financial, and legal text.
metrics.measures: How often the answer says the opposite of the source.

use_cases: any place a contradiction is worse than an omission
signals: A contradiction would cause harm or a mis-sale
You already measure faithfulness and want the contradiction slice
NLI labels or a judge can mark contradiction separately from neutral

when_not_to_use: You only need one grounding number. Faithfulness is enough. Add this only when the client treats contradiction as a different severity.
There is no source. Contradicting the world is hallucination or factual_correctness, not this metric.

required_inputs.notes: Either an NLI model with a contradiction class or a judge with a three-way label. One of the two is required. Prefer NLI for cost.

computation.formula: contradiction_rate = contradictory_claims / claims. Lower is better.
procedure: Split the answer into claims.
Label each claim entailed, neutral, or contradictory against the source.
Report the contradictory fraction. Do not fold neutral 'not in source' claims into this rate.
implementations: A judge prompt with an explicit contradiction label

interpretation.meaning: No claim contradicts the source.
A strict gate for customer-visible regulated answers is often at or under a small rate like this. Set it from the client's risk, not from a default.
Every claim contradicts the source.

score.aggregation: Mean over cases, plus the fraction of cases with any contradiction.
score.suggested_gate: <= 0.01 when a contradiction is a reportable incident.

cost_effort.driver: NLI labels, or a judge if NLI is not available.
cost_effort.notes: Cheap with a three-way NLI model. Do not pay a large judge unless the domain language breaks NLI.

limitations: Neutral and contradiction are easy to confuse on hedged sentences.
The rate ignores omissions. A silent answer scores well here and poorly on coverage.

metrics.name: Faithfulness
metrics.description: The share of claims in the answer that the retrieved context supports. This is the Ragas and DeepEval faithfulness metric and the claim-level form of groundedness. It is the default quality metric whenever the product must not speak beyond the passages it was given, including summaries.
metrics.measures: Whether the answer stays inside the supplied evidence. It does not measure whether that evidence is true or complete.

use_cases: summaries that must stay inside a source
support replies constrained to a help center
signals: The prompt says to answer only from the provided documents
Retrieved chunks or a source document are logged with the output
An unsupported sentence is worse than an incomplete answer

when_not_to_use: The product is supposed to add world knowledge on top of the documents. Faithfulness punishes true statements that are not in the context. Split grounded claims from allowed background.
You need to know whether retrieval found the right passages. A faithful answer can be grounded in the wrong document. Add context_recall or context_relevancy.

required_inputs.notes: No gold answer. Pass the question so the judge decomposes the claims that matter. HHEM-style NLI is the cheaper alternate groundedness_nli, not a second copy of this metric.

computation.formula: faithfulness = supported_claims / total_claims. Claims the context does not entail are unsupported. If the answer has no factual claims, define the score as 1 only when you also require answer_relevancy, and record that convention.
procedure: Split the answer into atomic claims.
Ask whether each claim is entailed by the retrieved context.
Divide supported claims by total claims. Store the verdicts with the run.

interpretation.meaning: Every claim is supported by the context.
The catalogue's default RAG gate. Confirm it matches the client's risk.
No claim is supported.

score.aggregation: Mean of per-case ratios. Also report the share of cases with any unsupported claim, which is hallucination at case level.
score.suggested_gate: >= 0.9 for regulated RAG and for summaries that feed a decision.

cost_effort.driver: One or two judge calls per case.
cost_effort.notes: The main RAG quality cost. Prefer groundedness_nli if you need a cheaper canary and keep this for the benchmark that ranks models.

limitations: Faithfulness can be perfect on an answer that is on the wrong topic, as long as it parrots the context. Pair with answer_relevancy.
Judges miss subtle numeric contradictions. Spot-check money, dates, and doses.

metrics.name: NLI groundedness
metrics.description: A natural-language inference model scores whether the answer is entailed by the source. Vectara's HHEM-2.1-Open is the widely used open model for this. It is the cheap alternate to judge-based faithfulness, not a second construct to average into Q alongside it.
metrics.measures: Entailment of the answer by the source, estimated by a fixed NLI model.

use_cases: RAG answers when judge budget is tight
signals: You need grounding on every run and cannot pay a large judge
The source document is logged
Faithfulness is the construct and you want a cheaper estimator

when_not_to_use: You are already running faithfulness with a pinned judge. Averaging the two double-counts grounding.
Answers are much longer than the NLI model's window. Chunk and aggregate explicitly or the score is an accident of truncation.

required_inputs.notes: Pin the NLI checkpoint. Do not swap HHEM for an instruction-tuned chat model and still call it this metric.

computation.formula: score = P_entail(answer | source), or the mean of per-sentence entailment probabilities. Range 0–1.
procedure: Split the answer into sentences if it exceeds the model window.
Score entailment against the source.
Aggregate by the minimum sentence if any unsupported sentence should fail the case, or by the mean if you want a soft score. Declare which.
implementations: AlignScore or MiniCheck as documented substitutes

interpretation.meaning: The NLI model is confident the answer is entailed. Confirm against a small human sample before treating it as a gate.
Uncertain entailment. Do not read this as 'half the facts are true'.
The NLI model sees no entailment.

score.aggregation: Mean over cases of the chosen sentence aggregation.

cost_effort.driver: A local or small NLI model, no general-purpose judge.
cost_effort.notes: The cheap grounding canary recommended when faithfulness is too expensive for every commit.

limitations: NLI models have their own blind spots on numbers, negation, and domain jargon.
A high score does not mean the answer addressed the question.

metrics.name: Noise sensitivity
metrics.description: How often the answer repeats incorrect claims that came from irrelevant retrieved chunks. Ragas defines this as a rate, so lower is better. A model that is distracted by distractor passages scores poorly even if it is fluent.
metrics.measures: The fraction of claims that are wrong because the model used noisy context.

use_cases: comparing models under a fixed noisy retriever
signals: Retrieved sets routinely contain irrelevant passages
You have seen the model quote the wrong chunk
A reference answer exists so you can tell a claim is incorrect

when_not_to_use: Retrieval is clean and you only need grounding. Faithfulness is the primary number. Noise sensitivity needs a notion of which chunks are noise and which claims are wrong.
You are tempted to treat a high score as good. The direction is lower-better. Do not drop it into Q without the one-minus transform, and prefer it as a diagnostic.

required_inputs.notes: The judge needs the question, the answer, the chunks labeled or inferred as noise, and the reference.

computation.formula: noise_sensitivity = incorrect_claims_attributed_to_noise / total_claims. Lower is better.
procedure: Identify claims in the answer that contradict the reference.
Attribute those incorrect claims to noisy chunks when the chunk supports the error.
Divide by the number of claims. Keep the score off the main quality average unless transformed.

interpretation.meaning: No claim was an error introduced by noisy context.
One in five claims is a distractor error. Too high for a regulated answer.
Every claim is an error traced to noise.

score.aggregation: Mean over cases. Never rank this higher-better.
score.suggested_gate: <= 0.05 when distractors are common and the answer is customer-visible.

cost_effort.driver: Claim judgments plus attribution to chunks.
cost_effort.notes: More expensive than faithfulness. Use it on a noise stress set, not on every happy-path case.

limitations: Attribution of an error to a specific chunk is ambiguous when several chunks overlap.
The score is only as good as the reference. A wrong reference creates phantom noise errors.

metrics.name: Math equivalence
metrics.description: The predicted answer is mathematically equal to the reference, so 0.5, 1/2, and 0.50 can all pass. Use it for quantitative client tasks: invoice checks, dosage math, eligibility arithmetic, and worked numerical answers.
metrics.measures: Equality of the final numeric or symbolic answer, not the elegance of the reasoning.

signals: The gold answer is a number, percentage, date offset, or short expression
Superficial string match would fail on formatting of the same quantity
The prompt asks the model to calculate rather than retrieve a phrase

when_not_to_use: Any number in a range is acceptable. Use numeric_tolerance_accuracy.
You need every intermediate step to be valid. A right answer can follow a wrong proof. Add step_correctness.

required_inputs.notes: Config sets absolute and relative tolerances and the unit. A small symbolic parser compares expressions. No judge required.

computation.formula: score = 1 if |pred - gold| <= atol + rtol*|gold| after unit conversion, or if a symbolic simplifier reduces pred - gold to 0.
procedure: Extract the final answer from the output using the configured pattern or JSON field.
Normalize units and percents.
Compare numerically or symbolically. Unparseable answers score 0.
implementations: MATH / Hendrycks answer normalization, adapted to client items
sympy equivalence where expressions are in scope
lm-evaluation-harness gsm8k exact match is the stricter special case

interpretation.meaning: The final answer matches within tolerance.
A typical target when the number drives a downstream decision.
The answer was missing, unparseable, or outside tolerance.

score.suggested_gate: >= 0.99 when an off-by amount causes a wrong payment or dose and the items are unambiguous.

cost_effort.notes: Cheap. Most failures are extraction of the final number, so log the extracted value.

limitations: Equivalence does not check the method. Add step_correctness when the work must be shown.
Unit conversion errors look like wrong math. Configure units explicitly.

metrics.name: Reasoning-trace faithfulness
metrics.description: Whether the written rationale actually supports the answer the model committed to, and does not cite tools, numbers, or policies that were not in the input. A persuasive but fabricated rationale fails. This is distinct from step_correctness, which asks whether the steps are mathematically valid.
metrics.measures: Support relationship between the visible rationale and the final answer, given only the provided evidence.

use_cases: answers that show their work to customers
signals: The UI shows a rationale next to a decision
The prompt says to justify from the case file only
You have seen fluent explanations that do not match the decision

when_not_to_use: No rationale is stored. Do not ask a judge to imagine one.
You only care that the final label is correct. Use the task metric.

required_inputs.notes: Pass the answer and the rationale separately when the product stores them apart. The source is the case file or tool results.

computation.formula: score = supported_rationale_claims / rationale_claims. A claim that the answer contradicts is unsupported.
procedure: Split the rationale into claims.
Mark each claim supported by the input, contradicted, or invented.
Score the supported fraction. Report contradiction separately via contradiction_rate when the source is a document.
implementations: Faithfulness-style claim checks applied to the rationale

interpretation.meaning: Every rationale claim is backed by the input and consistent with the answer.
A reasonable bar for explanations a customer will read.
The rationale is unsupported or fights the answer.

score.suggested_gate: >= 0.9 when the rationale is customer-visible in a regulated decision.

cost_effort.driver: One judge pass over the rationale.
cost_effort.notes: Similar cost to faithfulness. Do not also run a generic rubric on the same claims.

limitations: The metric cannot see hidden chain-of-thought that the API does not return.
Judges sometimes accept specific-sounding numbers. Spot-check finance and dose explanations.

metrics.name: Self-consistency rate
metrics.description: How often independent samples of the same item agree on the final answer. High agreement is evidence the model is stable on that item. It is not evidence the agreed answer is true. Use it as a reliability companion to a correctness metric.
metrics.measures: Stability of the decoded answer across repeats, after answer normalization.

use_cases: decisions you might otherwise take from a single sample
detecting items that need a larger sample or a tool
signals: The runner already repeats each case
Temperature or reasoning effort is above greedy decoding
You plan to majority-vote samples in production

when_not_to_use: There is no correctness metric. A model can be consistently wrong. Do not rank by agreement alone.
The task is open-ended prose. Exact agreement is the wrong equivalence. Cluster with semantic equivalence or use flip_rate on a pass bit.

required_inputs.notes: Needs at least 3 samples. Config defines answer extraction. No gold label required, which is why this cannot enter Q by itself.

computation.formula: For each case, score = count(samples equal to the majority answer) / n_samples. The run score is the mean. Ties use the smallest tied answer so the rate is defined.
procedure: Extract a canonical answer from each sample.
Find the majority answer and the agreement rate.
Report agreement beside accuracy. Low agreement plus high accuracy means the pass is fragile.

interpretation.meaning: Every sample agreed.
A 2-of-3 majority. Acceptable only if the agreed answer is also correct.
No real consensus at three samples.

cost_effort.driver: Extra samples you may already be paying for in repeats.
cost_effort.notes: Free if repeats exist. Do not launch a new sample budget only for this number.

limitations: Agreement is not truth. Pair with math_equivalence, exact_match, or another gold metric.
The rate depends on temperature, reasoning effort, and provider nondeterminism.

metrics.name: Step correctness
metrics.description: The fraction of intermediate steps that are valid, given the problem and the preceding valid steps. A correct final answer with a broken derivation scores poorly. Use it when an analyst, clinician, or auditor will read the work.
metrics.measures: Validity of the reasoning trace, step by step, separate from the final answer.

signals: The product shows the chain of thought or a rationale to a person
A right number reached by a wrong rule would be unacceptable
References include a solution sketch, or a judge can apply a domain rule

when_not_to_use: Only the final value is consumed by code. Score math_equivalence and do not pay for steps.
The model is instructed to hide reasoning. You would be grading text the product does not use.

required_inputs.notes: A reference sketch is optional. Without it, the judge applies configured domain rules and marks each step valid, invalid, or irrelevant.

computation.formula: score = valid_steps / max(1, relevant_steps). Irrelevant filler is excluded from the denominator and reported separately.
procedure: Split the trace into steps with a deterministic segmenter or the judge.
Label each step valid or invalid given the prompt and earlier valid steps.
Compute the fraction. Also report whether the final answer matches, but do not mix it into this score.
implementations: Process reward models and PRM800K-style step labels
A rubric judge with one verdict per step

interpretation.meaning: Every relevant step checked out.
Mostly sound work with some broken steps. Read those steps before shipping.
No relevant step was valid.

cost_effort.driver: A judge call that must see every step.
cost_effort.notes: Several times a normal rubric call on long traces. Skip it when the trace is not user-visible.

limitations: Judges prefer fluent, long traces. Cap length or the score tracks verbosity.
A valid-looking step can still be unfaithful to the model's actual computation. See reasoning_trace_faithfulness.

metrics.name: Empty-output rate
metrics.description: The share of calls that return success with no content and no tool call. It is a component of error_rate. Empty bodies are a known provider and safety-filter behavior and they should not be scored as a wrong answer without being counted here.
metrics.measures: Successful responses with nothing in them.

use_cases: safety filters that return empty rather than a refusal
signals: Empty completions appear in logs
A safety filter may blank the output

when_not_to_use: A deliberate empty field is valid in the schema. Define empty as no content and no tool call, not as a null JSON field.
As a second gate beside error_rate by default.

required_inputs.notes: Counted inside catalogue error_rate. Broken out here for diagnosis.

computation.formula: empty_output_rate = calls with an empty completion and no tool call / calls.
procedure: Inspect the body of HTTP 200 responses.
Count empties.
If a safety filter is the cause, also look at safety metrics rather than only reliability.

interpretation.meaning: No empty successes.
Empty bodies are common enough to move quality numbers if you score them as ordinary wrong answers.

cost_effort.notes: Free diagnostic computed from logs the runner already stores.

limitations: Some empty bodies are refusals with a finish reason of content_filter. Split that reason if the provider sends it.
Tool-only turns are not empty.
provenance: Component of the BIY error rate

metrics.name: Error rate
metrics.description: The share of calls that fail: HTTP errors, timeouts, and empty completions. This is the catalogue metric error_rate. It is always measured and it is the default reliability gate. Timeouts and empty bodies are also broken out so a single rate is diagnosable.
metrics.measures: Calls that did not return a usable completion.

signals: Every run
A hard reliability gate or a provider comparison

when_not_to_use: As a quality metric. A successful HTTP call can still be a wrong answer.
To hide throttling. throttle_rate is separate so a rate limit is not called slowness or a model error.

required_inputs.notes: Catalogue definition: HTTP errors, timeouts, and empty completions. Throttles are excluded and counted in throttle_rate. Catalogue id error_rate.

computation.formula: error_rate = (http_errors + timeouts + empty_completions) / calls.
procedure: Classify each call.
Exclude 429s from this rate.
Gate on the combined rate and show the components.

interpretation.meaning: About one failure in a hundred. The architecture's example gate is at or under 0.01, and chat defaults to 0.02.
The catalogue's looser batch default. Still a lot of failed work.

score.suggested_gate: <= 0.02 for chat and <= 0.01 when a failure breaks a user-visible action. Batch may use <= 0.05.

cost_effort.notes: Always measured from logs the runner already stores. No extra model call.

limitations: A provider that returns a 200 with an error payload will be missed unless you inspect the body.
Timeouts depend on the client's timeout setting. Publish that setting.

metrics.name: Flip rate
metrics.description: The share of cases whose pass or fail bit is not the same across repeats. This is the catalogue metric flip_rate. Temperature 0 is not deterministic on shared inference. A high flip rate means a single sample is a weak basis for a recommendation. Lower is better.
metrics.measures: Instability of the pass bit across repeats.

use_cases: deciding whether a close quality gap is real
signals: Repeats are at least 2
Two candidates are close
Temperature or provider noise is non-trivial

when_not_to_use: You ran one sample. The rate is undefined. Do not report zero.
As a substitute for pass_hat_k on agents. Flip rate is about the pass bit. pass_hat_k is about succeeding every trial.

required_inputs.notes: The pass bit is the task's success definition. Catalogue id flip_rate. Needs at least two repeats.

computation.formula: flip_rate = cases where the pass bit is not unanimous across repeats / cases.
procedure: Score each repeat.
Mark a case as flipped if both pass and fail appear.
Report the rate with the repeat count.
implementations: The research note on inference nondeterminism

interpretation.meaning: Every case was stably pass or stably fail.
One in five cases flips. A small quality gap between models is not actionable without more repeats.

cost_effort.notes: Free given the default three repeats. Do not add repeats only for this number until a decision depends on stability.

limitations: The rate depends on how generous the pass bit is.
Three repeats only detect coarse instability.
provenance: Thinking Machines on inference nondeterminism, as cited in the research note

metrics.name: pass^k
metrics.description: The probability that every one of k independent trials of a task succeeds. This is the catalogue metric pass_hat_k and the τ-bench reliability metric. pass@k asks whether any sample works. pass^k asks whether the agent works every time, which is the right question for a side-effecting or customer-facing action.
metrics.measures: Consistent success across k trials of the same task.

use_cases: any task a user will retry and expect to work again
signals: The kind is agent
Repeats exist
A flaky success is not acceptable

when_not_to_use: The product can screen samples and keep a passing one, as in offline code generation. pass_at_k matches that workflow better.
k is larger than the number of repeats. The unbiased estimate is then mostly zeros. Pick k no greater than n.

required_inputs.notes: n repeats, c successes, k the reliability horizon. Catalogue id pass_hat_k. Default k is the number of repeats when that is 3.

computation.formula: pass^k = mean over tasks of C(c, k) / C(n, k). The term is 0 when c < k.
procedure: Score each repeat as success or not.
Apply the unbiased estimator per task.
Average over tasks. For k = 1 this equals the mean success rate.

interpretation.meaning: Every task succeeded on enough trials that all k-subsets pass.
Only half of tasks are reliable at this k. A 70 percent single-trial success often collapses here as k grows.
No task succeeded on k trials.

score.aggregation: Unweighted mean of the per-task estimator.

cost_effort.notes: With the default three repeats, report pass^1 and pass^3. Do not launch n=8 unless reliability is the decision.

limitations: The estimator assumes i.i.d. trials. Shared prefixes and caches violate that.
A strict success bit makes pass^k harsh, which is the point for agents.

metrics.name: Throttle rate
metrics.description: The share of calls that received HTTP 429 at the concurrency you actually configured. This is the catalogue metric throttle_rate. It is recorded separately so throttling is not counted as model latency. Lower is better.
metrics.measures: Rate-limit responses at the benchmark's concurrency.

signals: Every run against a rate-limited API
Choosing a concurrency for the provider

when_not_to_use: As a model-quality score. It is a property of the account, the concurrency, and the provider.
After silent client retries that hide the 429. Count the 429 even if a retry succeeded, or you will understate the limit.

required_inputs.notes: Catalogue id throttle_rate. Config concurrency is part of the result.

computation.formula: throttle_rate = calls with HTTP 429 / calls, measured at the configured concurrency.
procedure: Count 429 responses before retry.
Publish concurrency beside the rate.
Do not fold this into e2e_ms.

interpretation.meaning: The configured concurrency stayed inside the limit during the run.
One in ten calls was limited. Latency and throughput from this run are not steady-state numbers.

score.suggested_gate: <= 0.01 at the concurrency you intend to run in production.

cost_effort.notes: Always measured from logs the runner already stores. No extra model call.

limitations: A quiet hour and a busy hour differ. The research note on time of day applies.
Some gateways return 503 for the same condition. Map provider-specific limit statuses into this rate and document the map.

metrics.name: Timeout rate
metrics.description: The share of calls that hit the client timeout. It is a component of error_rate, reported on its own because a timeout epidemic is a latency and capacity problem, not the same bug as a 500.
metrics.measures: Calls aborted for exceeding the client timeout.

signals: error_rate moved and you need the component
prompts are long
timeouts appear in logs

when_not_to_use: As an additional gate on top of error_rate without a reason. The combined gate is the default. This is the breakdown.
With an unpublished timeout. The rate is then incomparable.

required_inputs.notes: The timeout threshold is config and must be stamped. These calls are also inside error_rate.

computation.formula: timeout_rate = timed_out_calls / calls.
procedure: Count client timeouts.
Publish the threshold.
Do not also add this rate into Q.

interpretation.meaning: No call hit the timeout.
Five percent timed out. Latency percentiles that drop these calls are biased.

cost_effort.notes: Free diagnostic computed from logs the runner already stores.

limitations: A short client timeout manufactures a high rate.
Server-side timeouts may arrive as 504. Map them and say so.
provenance: Component of the BIY error rate

metrics.name: Truncation rate
metrics.description: The share of calls whose finish reason is length, meaning the model hit the output cap before finishing. This is the catalogue metric truncation_rate. Always measured. A truncated JSON object is both a truncation and a schema failure.
metrics.measures: Completions cut off by the output limit.

signals: Every run
max_tokens is set

when_not_to_use: As evidence the model is verbose by preference. It may be hitting a cap you set too low. Raise the cap in a diagnostic before blaming the model.
As a quality score. Truncation is a reliability failure. A short complete answer is not better merely because it avoided the cap.

required_inputs.notes: finish_reason == length. Catalogue id truncation_rate.

computation.formula: truncation_rate = calls with finish_reason length / calls.
procedure: Read finish_reason.
Count length finishes.
If the rate is high, rerun a slice with a higher cap before ranking models.

interpretation.meaning: No call hit the output cap.
One in twenty calls is cut off. Structured output will be failing with it.

score.suggested_gate: <= 0.01 when the caller cannot repair a partial payload.

cost_effort.notes: Always measured from logs the runner already stores. No extra model call.

limitations: Some providers use a different reason string. Map it explicitly.
A high cap that is still hit is a model behavior. A low cap is a config. Record max_tokens.

metrics.name: Long-context accuracy
metrics.description: Task accuracy at the context length the product actually uses. Advertised context windows are not effective context. RULER and needle-in-a-haystack evaluations showed large drops inside the claimed window. Score the client's task at the client's length, and use a synthetic needle only as a diagnostic.
metrics.measures: Quality at the production context length.

signals: Typical prompts are long
The product depends on finding a fact buried in a document
You are choosing among long-context models

when_not_to_use: Production prompts are short. A needle test will not change the decision and costs a lot of tokens.
You substitute a public RULER score for the client's task. Public scores are a prior. This metric is the client's task at the client's length.

required_inputs.notes: Build items at the target length by using real documents where possible. A synthetic needle subset may be added and must be reported separately.

computation.formula: The primary task metric, computed only on items in the target length bucket. Needle diagnostic = retrieved needles / planted needles.
procedure: Bucket items by input length.
Compute the task metric in the bucket that matches production.
If a needle diagnostic is included, report it beside the task metric, not instead of it.
implementations: RULER-style length sweeps on client tasks

interpretation.meaning: The task metric is perfect at the production length.
A large drop from the short-context score. The window is not effectively usable at this length.
The task fails at the production length.

score.aggregation: The task metric within the length bucket.
score.suggested_gate: No more than a client-set drop from the short-context score.

cost_effort.driver: Long prompts, often the dominant token cost of the whole benchmark.
cost_effort.notes: One length bucket at the real p95 input length is more informative than a sweep the client will not use.

limitations: Needle retrieval is easier than multi-hop use of long context. Do not stop at needles.
Truncation by the provider looks like a model failure. Record the served context length.

metrics.name: Lost-in-the-middle drop
metrics.description: The drop in accuracy when the relevant passage sits in the middle of the context rather than at the start or the end. Liu and colleagues documented this U-shaped curve. Lower drop is better. Use it when retrieval packs many chunks and the answer is often not in the first or last one.
metrics.measures: Position sensitivity of long-context accuracy.

use_cases: long context where the relevant span is not pinned to the edge
signals: Prompts contain many chunks
You cannot guarantee the relevant chunk is first
long_context_accuracy is in scope

when_not_to_use: The product always puts the relevant document first and the rest is not used as evidence. Position will not vary.
As a substitute for retrieval quality. If the chunk is absent, position is not the bug. Check context_recall.

required_inputs.notes: The same item is run with the relevant chunk placed at the start, middle, and end. Placements are frozen.

computation.formula: drop = accuracy_at_edges - accuracy_at_middle, where edges are the mean of start and end. Stored drop is clipped at 0. Lower is better.
procedure: Run the three placements.
Score each with the task metric.
Subtract. A negative raw drop means the middle was easier. Store 0 and show the raw curve.
implementations: Lost in the Middle (Liu et al., 2023)

interpretation.meaning: Middle placement was no worse than the edges.
A material position effect. Reranking or chunk budget matters more than the generator.
Edge accuracy is perfect and middle accuracy is zero on this set.

cost_effort.notes: Run on a small diagnostic set once you know long context matters.

limitations: The synthetic placement can differ from how the retriever orders real chunks.
A small item set makes a noisy drop. Report the item count.
provenance: Liu et al., 2023, Lost in the Middle

metrics.name: Negation robustness
metrics.description: Accuracy on items that differ from a positive item by a negation the model must respect. Models often answer the positive question they expected. Higher is better. Use it for policies, eligibility, and clinical contraindications, where 'not' changes the decision.
metrics.measures: Whether the model respects negation that flips the correct answer.

signals: Rules contain not, except, or unless
You have seen the model ignore a negation
Paired positive and negative items can be written

when_not_to_use: Negation does not change the label in this domain. Then the test is artificial.
Pairs are generated carelessly and the negated item is ungrammatical or ambiguous.

required_inputs.notes: Pairs are human-reviewed. Score the negated items. Also report whether the model gave the same answer as on the positive twin, which is the failure pattern.

computation.formula: negation_accuracy = correct_negated_items / negated_items.
procedure: Run positive and negated twins.
Score the negated items against their own labels.
Report the rate of copied positive answers.

interpretation.meaning: Every negated item was answered correctly.
Negation is a real gap. Do not ship a rule engine on top of this model without a checker.
No negated item was correct.

score.suggested_gate: >= 0.95 when a missed negation changes eligibility or a contraindication.

cost_effort.notes: The pairs are the cost. Keep them few and sharp.

limitations: Double negatives and scope ambiguity make items unfair. Review them.
High accuracy on negated items can coexist with low accuracy on ordinary items. Report both.

metrics.name: Option-order sensitivity
metrics.description: How much a multiple-choice or ranked decision changes when the options are permuted. Lower is better. Position bias is a known judge and model failure. If the product presents options, this belongs in the benchmark.
metrics.measures: Dependence of the answer on the order of options.

use_cases: judges that pick between two model outputs
signals: The prompt lists options
You suspect the model picks the first or last option
You are also using a pairwise judge

when_not_to_use: There are no options. Order of retrieved documents is lost_in_the_middle_drop, a different test.
The order is meaningful, such as a procedure. Permuting it changes the task.

required_inputs.notes: Permutations are frozen. For pairwise judges this is why the catalogue runs both orders.

computation.formula: sensitivity = items whose predicted label changes across permutations / items. Lower is better.
procedure: Run each frozen permutation.
Map answers back to option identities, not positions.
Score the item as sensitive if any permutation disagrees.
implementations: Pairwise judging in both orders, as in the BIY judge notes

interpretation.meaning: No item changed its choice when options moved.
One in ten items is order-dependent. Too high for a judge or a high-stakes choice.
Every item changed with order.

score.suggested_gate: <= 0.05 for a judge used to rank models, and for customer-facing option pickers.

cost_effort.notes: Two orders are enough to catch a first-position bias in pairwise judging.

limitations: A model can be consistently wrong and order-stable.
Many permutations on few items make a noisy rate. Freeze a small permutation set.
provenance: Position bias in multiple choice and in LLM judges

metrics.name: Paraphrase invariance
